newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- South Africans would soon require a tax certificate to buy foreign currency or apply for government tenders, and the system could be extended to include home electricity connections and financial transactions such as opening a bank account, the SA Revenue Service said on Monday.

- The African National Congress has told the truth commission it killed informers and apartheid government agents, violated legal and human rights of detainees suspected of working for the government, waited too long before condemning necklace murders and carried out at least 500 military actions inside SA.

- Government was unlikely to meet the employment growth targets set out in its macroeconomic strategy after disappointing growth in the manufacturing sector last year, finance department deputy director-general Andre Roux said on Monday.
- The Public Service Commission released a draft code of conduct on Monday to help stamp out corruption in the public service and provide a better service to the public.
- The Inkatha Freedom Party has sacked Mike Tarr as IFP chief whip in the KwaZulu Natal legislature, allegedly because of his failure to support the party's push for Ulundi as provincial capital.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Gold hit its highest level for more than a month on Monday, spurred by a fall in the value of the dollar against the yen, traders said.

- A draft of next year's national and provincial expenditure budgets will be published in November for comment by parliament, Nedlac and the Financial and Fiscal Commission, Trevor Manuel, the finance minister, said on Monday.

- A total of $1 billion due to Telkom, the telecommunications utility, following its part privatisation, has been sold forward for delivery on May 22 or shortly after, a finance ministry official said on Monday.

- Several new polypropylene plants, which are due to come on stream towards the end of the year, will lead to a growing oversupply on world markets, which could depress prices by up to 30 percent, industry sources and analysts said on Monday.

- Gary Player Golf Equipment, a division of the Gary Player Group, has signed an exclusive brand licensing and distribution agreement with Leisure Net's golfing subsidiary, the Pro Shop, Marc Player, the chief executive of the group said on Monday.
THE STAR

- The leadership of the ANC overruled a plot from within its ranks to assassinate IFP leader Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki told the Truth and Reconciliation Commission on Monday.
- ANC soldiers in camps outside South Africa committed "gender-specific" offences against their female comrades because it was too dangerous for the men to go into town.
- Johannesburg's new Wall of Remembrance, to honour the memory of those murdered during brutal crimes, has drawn widespread backing.
- Seven climbers were feared dead after a severe storm stranded them just below the summit of Mount Everest, mountaineers said on Monday.
- Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi told Parliament on Monday that more than 333 000 people had been arrested as part of the Sword and Shield anti-crime campaign, which ended in March.
- The Gauteng legislature on Monday adopted a motion to increase vehicle licence fees by 20 percent adding to the province's revenue by 60 million rand.
